## ErrorBoundaryProps

```typescript
interface ErrorBoundaryProps
```

What an `ErrorBoundary` takes.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | field | `ReactNode` | The subtree this boundary guards. |
| `fallback` | field | `(error: Error, reset: () => void) => ReactNode` | Shown instead of the subtree. Receives the error and a function that clears the boundary and remounts the children. |
| `onError` | field | `(error: Error, info: ErrorInfo) => void` | Somewhere to send this — a logger, telemetry, a toast. |
| `resetKeys` | field | `readonly unknown[]` | Changing any of these clears the boundary. |

## ErrorBoundary

```typescript
class ErrorBoundary extends Component<ErrorBoundaryProps, State>
```

What is shown where a subtree threw.

See the note at the top of this file: it catches less than people
expect, and the default fallback shows the message on purpose.

**Also** [`ErrorBoundaryProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#errorboundaryprops).

| Member | Kind | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | field | `State` |
| `getDerivedStateFromError` | method | `(error: Error) => State` |
| `componentDidCatch` | method | `(error: Error, info: ErrorInfo) => void` |
| `componentDidUpdate` | method | `(previous: ErrorBoundaryProps) => void` |
| `render` | method | `() => ReactNode` |

## ToastOptions

```typescript
interface ToastOptions
```

What a toast says and how long it stays.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tone` | field | `Tone` | How loud it is. `danger` interrupts; the rest wait for a pause. |
| `duration` | field | `number | null` | Milliseconds before it goes. `null` keeps it until dismissed, which is the default when there is an `action`. |
| `action` | field | `ReactNode` | One thing to do about it. Keeps the toast until dismissed. |

## Toast

interface Toast extends ToastOptions

| `id` | field | `string` | Its id, so it can be dismissed early. |
| `message` | field | `ReactNode` | What it says. |

## ToastApi

```typescript
interface ToastApi
```

How to raise and dismiss toasts.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `show` | field | `(message: ReactNode, options?: ToastOptions) => string` | Show one. Returns its id, so it can be dismissed early. |
| `dismiss` | field | `(id: string) => void` | Take one away before its time is up. |
| `clear` | field | `() => void` | Take every one away. |

## ToastHost

```typescript
function ToastHost({ children }: { children: ReactNode })
```

Wrap the part of the app that raises toasts.

Renders the stack itself, so there is nothing to place and no way
to forget to place it.

## useToast

```typescript
function useToast(): ToastApi
```

Raise a toast.

Throws outside a `ToastHost` rather than returning a no-op.
A silent no-op here means a save that reports success by showing
nothing, which looks exactly like a save that did not happen.

**Also** [`ToastApi`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#toastapi).

## Banner

```typescript
function Banner({ tone = "neutral", onDismiss, children, className, ...rest }: BannerProps)
```

A condition that is still true.

Not a toast: a toast is about something that just happened and
goes away, a banner is about a state — offline, read-only, licence
expiring — and stays until the state does not.

**Also** [`BannerProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#bannerprops).

## Announcer

```typescript
interface Announcer
```

A live region and the function that speaks into it.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `announce` | field | `(message: string, urgency?: Urgency) => void` | Say something. Re-saying the same thing still announces. |
| `region` | field | `React.ReactElement` | Render this. It must be in the tree before anything is said. |

## useAnnounce

```typescript
function useAnnounce(): Announcer
```

A live region and the function that speaks into it.

Two regions are rendered, not one. A single region whose
`aria-live` value changes is unreliable: the attribute is read
when the region is observed, so flipping it at the same moment the
text changes races, and the announcement comes out at whichever
urgency the implementation noticed first.

**Also** [`Announcer`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#announcer).

## LiveRegion

```typescript
function LiveRegion({ children = "", urgency = "polite" }: LiveRegionProps)
```

The declarative form, for a value that already lives in state.

`<LiveRegion>{`${n} results`}</LiveRegion>` is the whole usage.
Mounted empty on the first render so the region exists before it
has anything to say — see note 1 above.

**Also** [`LiveRegionProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-feedback#liveregionprops).
